gaps.sentence: 'The train left ten minutes ago,' she said. She said the train ___ ten minutes before.
gaps.explanation: Past simple becomes past perfect, and 'ago' becomes 'before': had left ten minutes before.

gaps.sentence: 'You really ought to try the tasting menu,' the waiter said. The waiter ___ trying the tasting menu.
gaps.explanation: Recommend takes a gerund (recommend doing) when there is no object.

gaps.sentence: 'I'm meeting them tomorrow evening,' she said. She said she was meeting them ___ evening.
gaps.explanation: Tomorrow evening becomes the next (or the following) evening.

gaps.sentence: 'We might have missed the turning,' he admitted. He admitted that they ___ have missed the turning.
gaps.explanation: Might has no further backshift form, so it is unchanged.

gaps.sentence: 'I didn't take your charger,' she insisted. She ___ taking my charger.
gaps.explanation: Denials are reported as deny + -ing: denied taking.

gaps.sentence: 'Which seat do you prefer?' the steward asked. The steward asked which seat I ___.
gaps.explanation: do you prefer → I preferred: statement order, present simple backshifted.

gaps.sentence: 'I used to live in Cairo,' she mentioned. She mentioned that she ___ to live in Cairo.
gaps.explanation: 'Used to' has no backshift form; it remains used to after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: 'Come round to my house tomorrow,' she said. She invited me round to her house ___.
gaps.explanation: Tomorrow becomes the next day (the following day) when the invitation is reported.
